ITQAN:v3p171/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p171/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p171/r12.claim: The omitted result is that one would see a dreadful scene if the criminals were seen with bowed heads.
ITQAN:v3p171/r12.anchor: ﴿ ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رؤوسهم ﴾ أي لرأيت أمرا فظيعا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.claim: Those who reject resurrection will find their confession useless; belief after seeing the realities would negate the purpose of intellect and moral awareness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.anchor: a confession of sins by people will be of no avail to them on that day.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r1.claim: The Qur'an usually puts hearing before sight because hearing is more important for religious obligation and conveying a message: a blind person who hears can be reached, while a deaf person is harder to address.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r1.anchor: الأكثر في القرآن تقديم السمع على البصر لأن السمع أهم من البصر في التكليف والتبليغ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r2.claim: Hearing has a shorter range than sight, so a person we hear is usually closer than someone we see.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r2.anchor: مدى السمع أقل من مدى البصر فمن نسمعه يكون عادة أقرب ممن نراه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r3.claim: Hearing develops in a person before sight, another reason it is normally mentioned first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r3.anchor: السمع ينشأ في الإنسان قبل البصر في التكوين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r5.claim: In worldly life the criminals heard about resurrection but did not see it, leaving room for doubt; in the afterlife they see what they had heard, reaching certainty, so that realm fittingly foregrounds sight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r5.anchor: في الدنيا يسمعون عن القيامة وأحوالها ولا يبصرون لكن ما يسمعوه كان يدخل في مجال الشك والظنّ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p66/r6.claim: The author compares the certainty of direct sight to the saying that hearing news is not like seeing for oneself.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r1.claim: The generic example has no particular addressee: it describes how someone may respond badly when honored.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r1.anchor: فلا يريد به مخاطبا بعينه، وكأنك قلت: إن أكرم وإن أحسن إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r2.claim: The cited poem illustrates that لو can carry a conditional sense with an expressed answer, even when the condition is counterfactual.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r2.anchor: فلو نبش المقابر عن كليب ... فيخبر بالذنائب أي زير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says لو can convey a wish, as in wishing someone would come and speak with you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقد تجيء لو في معنى التمني، كقولك: لو تأتيني فتحدثني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says making لو desiderative here is far-fetched and calling it conditional is imprecise; even when it conveys a wish, it still has an answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r4.anchor: والتمني بلو في هذا الموضع بعيد، وتسمية لو امتناعية ليس بجيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r5.speaker: ابن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r5.claim: Ibn Malik says the example لو تأتيني فتحدثني is sound if it elides وددت, but لو is not inherently a particle of wishing, since it can follow تمنيت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r5.anchor: فقال ابن مالك: إن أراد به الحذف، أي وددت لو تأتيني فصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r6.claim: ناكسوا رؤوسهم means bowing their heads from humiliation, sadness, worry, grief, and disgrace.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r6.anchor: ناكسوا رؤسهم: مطرقوها، من الذل والحزن والهم والغم والذم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads نكسوا رؤوسهم as a past verb with an object, while the majority read an active participle in a possessive construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r7.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: نكسوا رؤوسهم، فعلا ماضيا ومفعولا والجمهور: اسم فاعل مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r8.claim: عند ربهم means before the Lord who will recompense them, where a wrongdoer feels intense shame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r8.anchor: عند ربهم: أي عند مجازاته، وهو مكان شدة الخجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an understood يقولون after ربنا and describes their cry as an appeal for return to worldly life after seeing and hearing the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r9.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري: يستغيثون بقولهم: ربنا أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب وسمعنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r10.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r10.claim: Al-Naqqash says إنا موقنون means they are now certain of resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r10.anchor: إنا موقنون: أي بالبعث، قاله النقاش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r11.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r11.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam glosses موقنون as believing what the Messenger said.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r11.anchor: وقيل: مصدقون بالذي قال الرسول، قاله يحيى بن سلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r12.claim: موقنون may reveal their confusion when they finally see and hear, or mean their doubts have now vanished because they failed to reflect in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r12.anchor: وموقنون: مشعر بالالتباس في الحال، أي حين أبصروا وسمعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p435/r13.claim: Another interpretation makes their statement a confession that worldly signs and messengers left them no excuse.

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.claim: The first half treats revelation, God, creation especially of human beings, and Resurrection and Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.anchor: The first half of the sūrah discusses revelation (vv. 2–3), God (vv. 4–6), creation,

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r3.claim: The criminals lower their heads in shame, admit that they now see what they denied and hear the messengers' truth, and ask to return to do good works.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r3.anchor: المجرمون } المشركون { ناكسوا رؤوسهم } مطأطئوها حياء من ربهم عز وجل

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r1.claim: The address may console the Messenger because the deniers hurt him with their denial.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r1.anchor: خطابا مع الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم تشفيا لصدره فإنهم كانوا يؤذونه بالتكذيب

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the address is general to everyone, like a conditional saying that is not intended for one particular person.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون عاما مع كل أحد كما يقول القائل إن فلانا كريم إن خدمته ولو لحظة

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r3.claim: Standing before their Lord intensifies their shame: a servant who wronged his lord and then stands before him feels the utmost embarrassment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r3.anchor: لبيان شدة الخجالة لأن الرب إذا أساء إليه المربوب

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r4.claim: The participle or verb meaning they are saying is omitted; this signals extreme shame, since one overwhelmed by shame cannot speak.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r4.anchor: وحذف يقولون إشارة إلى غاية خجالتهم لأن الخجل العظيم الخجالة لا يتكلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r5.claim: They say they witnessed the gathering and heard the Messenger, then ask to return to worldly life to do righteous deeds; their present certainty cannot benefit them because faith and good works are accepted during earthly accountability.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r5.anchor: أبصرنا الحشر وسمعنا قول الرسول فارجعنا إلى دار الدنيا لنعمل صالحا

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r6.claim: On this reading they claim they believe now, but ask to return because faith and righteous action only help during the period of earthly obligation; Razi says the request is false because afterlife faith and deeds are not accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r6.anchor: إنا في الحال آمنا ولكن النافع الإيمان والعمل الصالح

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, they deny having associated partners as in their claim that they were not polytheists, and say their fate resulted from failing to do good, not from disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#3/r7.anchor: فقالوا إن هذا الذي جرى علينا ما جرى إلا بسبب ترك العمل الصالح

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r1.claim: One reading takes the address “Couldst thou but see” as directed specifically to the Prophet; either way it expresses amazement at the disbelievers' Hereafter state.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r1.anchor: Couldst thou but see is an address directly to the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r2.claim: Another reading takes the address as general rather than directed specifically to the Prophet; either way it conveys amazement at the disbelievers' Hereafter state.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r2.anchor: a general address (R). In either case, it refers to the amazement

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r3.claim: The guilty have died, witnessed the Resurrection and Judgment they denied, and admitted their sin.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r3.anchor: seen the realities of Resurrection and Judgment that they had denied

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r4.claim: “We are certain” may mean that they now believe with certainty.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r4.anchor: We are certain, meaning they believe with certainty

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r5.claim: Alternatively, they may merely claim belief to try to escape punishment, as in their denial of idolatry elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r5.anchor: simply claiming to believe in order to avoid the punishment, as in 6:23

STUDYQURAN:32:12/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r6.claim: God refuses return requests: 35:37 answers with the time and warning already given, 23:100 calls the request mere words, and 6:28 says returnees would repeat their forbidden conduct.
STUDYQURAN:32:12/r6.anchor: God thus denies all such requests, because even if they were sent back, they would return to the very thing they had been forbidden

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r3.claim: The criminals are those who asked whether they would be recreated after dissolving into the earth.

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r4.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r4.claim: Al-Kawāshī says law and idh normally refer to the past but introduce the future here because its occurrence is certain.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r4.anchor: قال في "الكواشي" : لو وإذ للماضي ودخلتا على المستقبل هنا لأن المستقبل من فعله كالماضي لتحقق وقوعه

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r5.claim: Naks is turning something upside down; here the criminals bow their heads before God from shame, sorrow, and grief.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r5.anchor: النكس قلب الشيء على رأسه ، وبالفارسية : (سرفرو افكندن

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r6.claim: They claim to now see and hear and grasp visible and audible signs, whereas they were formerly blind and perceived nothing.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r6.anchor: أي : صرنا ممن يبصر ويسمع وحصل لنا الاستعداد لإدراك الآيات المبصرة والمسموعة

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r7.claim: Farjiʿnā asks to be returned to worldly life.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r7.anchor: فأرددنا إلى الدنيا من رجعه رجعا أي : رده وصرفه

BURSEVI:v7p87/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p87/r1.claim: They ask to return so they can do righteous deeds according to the signs they now perceive.

BURSEVI:v7p87/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p87/r2.claim: Innā mūqinūn means they are now certain.

BURSEVI:v7p87/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p87/r3.claim: Al-Irshād reads their words as claims that their hearts are sound and can understand and act on the signs; before, they claim, they did not reason.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : ادعاء منهم لصحة الأفئدة والاقتدار على فهم معاني الآيات والعمل بموجبها

BURSEVI:v7p87/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p87/r4.claim: The omitted conditional result is that the hearer would see a dreadful scene; the future event is cast as past in interpretation, as if finished.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r4.anchor: وجواب لو محذوف أي : لرأيت أمرا فظيعا فهذا الأمر مستقبل في التحقيق ماض بحسب التأويل

BURSEVI:v7p87/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p87/r5.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the criminals as worldly people who bowed toward low desires after standing with heads raised before God at the primordial covenant.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أهل الدنيا من المجرمين وكان جرمهم أنهم نكسوا رؤوسهم

BURSEVI:v7p87/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p87/r6.claim: Satan's adornment of desires made them bow naturally and pursue appetite like cattle; 7:179 is cited, and humans are more astray because they share animals' natural desire and also violate commands.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أهل الدنيا من المجرمين وكان جرمهم أنهم نكسوا رؤوسهم

BURSEVI:v7p87/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p87/r7.claim: Having lived with heads lowered toward desire, they die and rise in that state, overwhelmed by shame and bewilderment; confession comes too late.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r7.anchor: فكما عاشوا ناكسي رؤوسهم إلى شهوات الدنيا ماتوا فيما عاشوا فيه ثم حشروا على ما ماتوا عليه

BURSEVI:v7p87/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p87/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p87/r8.claim: The closing Persian verses urge repentance while the soul remains in the body and the tongue can still offer an excuse.
BURSEVI:v7p87/r8.anchor: كنونت كه شمست اشكى ببار زبان دردهانست عذرى بيار نه بيوسته باشد روان در بدن

TAB-FULL:v18p605/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r1.claim: The criminals bow their heads before God in shame for their past disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r1.anchor: حياء من ربهم، للذي سلف منهم من معاصيه في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p605/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r2.claim: They confess that they now see the punishment and hear the messengers’ truth, then ask to return to worldly life and obey God.
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r2.anchor: منك تصديق ما كانت رسلك تأمرنا به في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p605/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r3.claim: Their certainty is now knowledge of God’s oneness, exclusive worship, His power over life and death, and resurrection after death.
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r3.anchor: إنا قد أيقنا الآن ما كنا به في الدنيا جهالا من وحدانيتك، وأنه لا يصلح أن يعبد سواك

TAB-FULL:v18p605/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the criminals are grief-stricken and ashamed.
TAB-FULL:v18p605/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: قوله " {ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم} قال: قد حزنوا واستحيوا

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r3.claim: Nukūs al-ra's means lowering or bowing the head.

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r4.claim: The criminals specifically are deniers of resurrection, identified by the verse's conclusion and the definite article's anaphoric reference to them.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r4.anchor: والمراد بالمجرمين بقرينة ذيل الآية خصوص المنكرين للمعاد

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r5.claim: Their standing before their Lord echoes the earlier statement that they denied meeting him; now they face the encounter they could not admit.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r5.anchor: { عند ربهم } محاذاة لما تقدم من قوله

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r6.claim: They say they saw by direct vision and heard through obedience, now recognizing that salvation requires faith and righteous action.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r6.anchor: أبصرنا بالمشاهدة وسمعنا بالطاعة فارجعنا نعمل عملا صالحا

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r7.claim: At the encounter, shame and regret make deniers acknowledge what they rejected and beg to return: they have certainty but lack righteous deeds, and will not return.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r7.anchor: وقد حصل لهم الإيمان اليقيني وبقي العمل الصالح ولذا يعترفون باليقين ويسألون الرجوع إلى الدنيا

TABRISI:32:12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r4.claim: Naks means turning something upside down; the word for relapse in illness takes ḍamma, while an inverted arrow takes kasra.
TABRISI:32:12/r4.anchor: والنكس قلبك الشيء على رأسه ويقال في المرض النكس بضم النون وأما النكس بكسر النون

TABRISI:32:12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r5.claim: The object of “if you saw” may be omitted, meaning “the criminals when they lower their heads.”
TABRISI:32:12/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعول { ترى } محذوفا فيكون تقديره

TABRISI:32:12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r6.claim: Alternatively, “saw” is literal and governs “when,” as in the verse describing the delights one sees in Paradise.
TABRISI:32:12/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى لو رأيت ببصرك مثل قوله وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت نعيما

TABRISI:32:12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r7.claim: The conditional answer is omitted: seeing the criminals in that state would provide an overwhelming lesson.
TABRISI:32:12/r7.anchor: وجواب لو محذوف تقديره لو رأيت المجرمين على تلك الحالة رأيت ما تعتبر به

TABRISI:32:12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r8.claim: “Taste” is what is said to them, and the phrase about forgetting is a genitive description of their day.
TABRISI:32:12/r8.anchor: فذوقوا أي فيقال لهم: ذوقوا العذاب بنسيانكم وهذا في موضع جر

TABRISI:32:12-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12-15/r1.claim: At the Resurrection the criminals hang their heads in shame, regret, and humiliation as they stand before their Lord for judgment.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r1.anchor: أي يوم القيامة حين يكون المجرمون متطأطئي رؤوسهم ومطرقيها حياء وندما وذلا

TABRISI:32:12-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12-15/r2.claim: “Before their Lord” means when God Himself undertakes the reckoning of His creatures.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r2.anchor: عند ربهم } أي عندما يتولى الله سبحانه حساب خلقه

TABRISI:32:12-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12-15/r3.claim: “We have seen and heard” means they have seen the guidance and heard the truth.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r3.anchor: ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا } أي أبصرنا الرشد وسمعنا الحق

TABRISI:32:12-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:32:12-15/r4.claim: One alternative is that they have seen the truth of God's promise and heard confirmation of His messengers.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r4.anchor: وقيل: معناه أبصرنا صدق وعدك وسمعنا منك تصديق رسلك

TABRISI:32:12-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:32:12-15/r5.claim: Another alternative is that they were formerly like the blind and deaf but now see and hear.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه إنا قد كنا بمنزلة العمي فأبصرنا وبمنزلة الصم فسمعنا

TABRISI:32:12-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12-15/r6.claim: They ask to be returned to the world of religious responsibility so they can perform good deeds.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r6.anchor: فارجعنا } أي فارددنا إلى دار التكليف { نعمل صالحا } من الصالحات

TABRISI:32:12-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12-15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12-15/r7.claim: They now have certainty and no longer doubt any truth or the message.
TABRISI:32:12-15/r7.anchor: إنا موقنون } اليوم لا نرتاب شيئا من الحق والرسالة

THALABI:v7p329/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p329/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p329/r1.claim: The criminals bow their heads from shame for their past sins.
THALABI:v7p329/r1.anchor: أي مطأطئو رؤوسهم عند ربهم حياء منه للذي سلف من معاصيهم في الدنيا

THALABI:v7p329/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p329/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p329/r2.claim: They admit seeing what they denied and hearing the messengers' truth, and ask to return to earthly life to do good, now certain.
THALABI:v7p329/r2.anchor: يقولون: ربنا أبصرنا ما كنا به مكذبين وسمعنا منك تصديق ما أتتنا به رسلك فارجعنا فارددنا إلى الدنيا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

THALABI:v7p329/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p329/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p329/r3.claim: The conditional's omitted answer means you would see an extraordinary sight.
THALABI:v7p329/r3.anchor: وجواب لو مضمر مجازه: لرأيت العجب

THALABI:v7p329/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p329/r8.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v7p329/r8.claim: Kaʿb says angels, prophets, martyrs, and believers intercede at Judgment; Mercy then intercedes for anyone who once remembered, feared, hoped in, or prayed to God, and they leave the Fire.
THALABI:v7p329/r8.anchor: عن كعب قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة يقوم الملائكة فيشفعون، ثم يقوم الأنبياء فيشفعون، ثم يقوم الشهداء فيشفعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r1.claim: Although إذ usually refers to the past, here it reports a future event; al-Wahidi discusses the construction under the parallel verse about people halted before the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r1.anchor: إذ تكون للماضي، وهذا إخبار عما هو آت بعد، وذكرنا الكلام في هذا عند قوله: {ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r2.claim: Muqatil identifies the criminals here as the Meccan disbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r3.claim: They have bowed their heads; al-Wahidi explains that a regretful person lowers his head while thinking in confusion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r3.anchor: أي مطأطئوها. وقال [ابن عباس] (¬2): من الندامة (¬3). وذلك أن النادم من شأنه أن يطأطئ رأسه متفكرا متحيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says their heads are bowed out of regret.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi analyzes the construct phrase as implicitly separated, citing similar expressions such as ثاني عطفه and هديا بالغ الكعبة; he discusses the verse fully under 4:97.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r5.anchor: فالإضافة في قوله: {ناكسو رءوسهم} في تقدير الانفصال؛ لأنه لم يأت بعد لا (¬4) للماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r6.claim: Their plea means: we now see what we were ignorant of and hear what we denied; they ask to return to worldly life and do good by declaring there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r6.anchor: وقوله: {ربنا} أي: يقولون {ربنا أبصرنا} ما كنا نجهل، وسمعنا ما كنا ننكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says they become certain on that day of what they had denied.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r7.anchor: {إنا موقنون} يريد: أيقنوا ذلك اليوم ما كانوا ينكروا (¬5). قاله ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq says the conditional has an omitted answer: the addressee would see something that gives the utmost lesson.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وهذا متروك الجواب، والجواب: لرأيت ما يعتبر به غاية الاعتبار (¬7).

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r1.claim: The criminals who bow their heads before their Lord are the polytheists.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r2.claim: They bow their heads in disgrace and regret.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r3.claim: They say they have seen and heard only when sight and hearing can no longer benefit them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r3.anchor: سمعوا حين لم ينفعهم السمع، وأبصروا حين لم ينفعهم البصر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r4.claim: They beg to be sent back to the world.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r5.claim: They now know that what Muḥammad brought them is true.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p688/r5.anchor: بالذي أتانا به محمد أنه حق

QASHANI:32:11-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:32:11-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:32:11-12/r2.claim: Those still retaining a remnant of primordial light can see, hear, and wish to return despite being veiled and drawn downward by entrenched bodily dispositions; they do not remain eternally in Hell, but are corrected according to how deeply those dispositions are rooted and then return.
QASHANI:32:11-12/r2.anchor: وهؤلاء هم الذين لا يتخلدون في النار بل يعدلون بحسب رسوخ الهيئات ثم يرجعون

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r1.claim: Once the worldly trial ends, later faith and remorse have no value; everyone should use the opportunity before death and before facing the truth of God’s eternal knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r1.anchor: sınavın süresi sona erdikten sonra iman etmenin ve pişmanlık sergilemenin hiçbir değeri olmayacaktır; bu sebeple herkes ecel gelip çatmadan aklını başına toplamalı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r4.claim: Many verses and hadith say people are not punished for sins they did not commit, may be forgiven through valid repentance and similar means, and receive reward for every good deed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r4.anchor: kişinin işlemediği bir günahtan ötürü ceza görmeyeceği, hatta şartlarına uygun bir tövbe ve benzeri vesilelerle günahlarının bağışlanacağı, buna karşılık yaptığı her iyiliğin de karşılığını göreceği bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r6.claim: Although mujrimīn literally means criminals or sinners, context identifies those denying resurrection and admitting their disbelief in the afterlife, so the author renders it ‘unbelievers.’
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:12/r6.anchor: 12. âyette geçen mücrimîn kelimesinin sözlük anlamı “suçlular, günahkârlar” olmakla beraber, burada öncelikle –10 ve 11. âyetlerde belirtildiği üzere– öldükten sonra dirilmeyi inkâr edenlerden

BURHAN:v3p197/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r2.claim: In the scene of the criminals, ربنا is introduced as their unspoken address: they say, “Our Lord.”

BURHAN:v2p219/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p219/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p219/r3.claim: Some treat the verse's address as general like the preceding examples; others say it addresses the Prophet specifically and لو expresses his wish to see his enemies humbled after their hostility.
BURHAN:v2p219/r3.anchor: فقيل إنه من هذا الباب ومنعه قوم وقال الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v2p219/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p219/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p219/r4.claim: A further analysis takes لو as counterfactual with its answer omitted, approximately “you would see the worst condition anyone could see.”
BURHAN:v2p219/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون لو امتناعية وجوابها محذوف أي لرأيت أسوأ حال يرى

BURHAN:v3p182/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p182/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p182/r6.claim: Answers to لو and لولا are often omitted; here one may supply “you would see a wonder,” “their terrible fate,” or “their dreadful state,” depending on the context.
BURHAN:v3p182/r6.anchor: والسر في حذفه في هذه المواضع أنها لما ربطت إحدى الجملتين بالأخرى

ITQAN:v3p91/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.claim: Some خطاب is general rather than aimed at one listener; its scene is so evident that anyone capable of seeing is included in the address.
ITQAN:v3p91/r6.anchor: لم يقصد بذلك خطاب معين بل كل أحد وأخرج في صورة الخطاب لقصد العموم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r4.claim: The speech verb is omitted: the criminals say ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p137/r4.anchor: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسوا رؤسهم عند ربهم

NAHHAS:v3p293/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p293/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p293/r2.claim: The clause is parsed as a nominal sentence with subject and predicate.
NAHHAS:v3p293/r2.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر قال أبو إسحاق المخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مخاطبة لأمته

NAHHAS:v3p293/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p293/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p293/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the singular address to the Prophet speaks to the community, with the sense If you all were to see.
NAHHAS:v3p293/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق المخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مخاطبة لأمته والمعنى ولو ترون

NAHHAS:v3p293/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p293/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v3p293/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās instead takes the address directly to Muḥammad: if he saw the criminals, he would regret his earlier course; the response to law is omitted.
NAHHAS:v3p293/r4.anchor: ومذهب أبي العباس غير هذا وأن يكون المعنى يا محمد قل للمجرم ولو ترى إذ المجرمون

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r1.claim: One analysis makes لو a condition bringing another event; al-Zamakhshari calls it counterfactuality, with a result omitted.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r2.claim: Al-Shaykh contests al-Zamakhshari's view; al-Samin directs readers to al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r2.anchor: وناقشه الشيخ في ذلك. وقد تقدم في أول البقرة تحقيقه.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r3.claim: Another analysis takes لو as optative, as if saying if only you could see; whether it has a result is disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r3.anchor: الثاني: أنها للتمني. قال الزمخشري: كأنه قيل: وليتك ترى. وفيها إذا كانت للتمني خلاف: هل تقتضي جوابا أم لا؟

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari appears to leave optative لو without a result; al-Shaykh says it has one.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والصحيح/ أن لها جوابا ".

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r5.claim: Al-Samin cites a poem wishing Kulaib could be raised and speak.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r6.speaker: ابن مالك
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r6.claim: Ibn Malik says لو is not inherently optative; al-Zamakhshari's example requires omitted وددت.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r6.anchor: إن أراد به الحذف أي: وددت لو تأتيني فتحدثني فصحيح، وإن أراد أنها موضوعة له فليس بصحيح

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r7.claim: The addressee may be the Prophet or someone else.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r7.anchor: وهل المخاطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو غيره؟ خلاف.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r8.claim: إذ retains past sense because لو shifts the present into past; the past signifies a certain future, like أتى أمر الله.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r8.anchor: على بابها من المضي لأن " لو " تصرف المضارع للمضي.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats إذ as replacing إذا; al-Samin says this is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r9.anchor: وجعله أبو البقاء مما وقع فيه " إذ " موقع " إذا " ولا حاجة إليه.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r10.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r10.claim: The common reading is a participle annexed to its object.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r10.anchor: العامة على أنه اسم فاعل مضاف لمفعوله تخفيفا.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r11.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads نكسوا as a past verb with رؤوسهم as object.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r11.anchor: وزيد بن علي " نكسوا " فعلا ماضيا، " رؤوسهم " ، مفعول به.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r12.claim: ربنا depends on omitted قول and is circumstantial; al-Zamakhshari estimates الاستغاثة, but omitting قول is more common.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r12.anchor: قوله: " ربنا " على إضمار القول وهو حال. أي قائلين ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r13.claim: The verbs may have omitted objects or mean they became seeing and hearing.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r13.anchor: يجوز أن يكون المفعول مقدرا أي: أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب، وسمعنا ما كنا ننكر.

SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r14.claim: صالحا is a direct object or adjective of omitted verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:32:12/r14.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعولا به، وأن يكون نعت مصدر.

ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r2.claim: The conditional has no stated answer; the Prophet is addressed for humankind, as in plural-address wording elsewhere, with an implied lesson to see.
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r2.anchor: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء

ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r3.claim: The phrase has an implicit يقولون: they say, before ربنا أبصرنا.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r4.claim: Although Qur'anic usage usually puts hearing first because it matters more for communication, hearing has shorter range, and develops earlier, these passages put sight first.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r4.anchor: الأكثر في القرآن تقديم السمع على البصر لأن السمع أهم من البصر في التكليف والتبليغ

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r5.claim: For the cave narrative, sight is especially salient: the sleepers hid so people would not see them, while God sees them in the dark; this motivates sight-first wording.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p70/r5.anchor: مسألة البصر هنا أهم من السمع فاقتضى تقديم البصر على السمع في الآية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r2.claim: In 32:12 sight precedes hearing because the condemned had heard in worldly life and denied, but now see the punishment and truth; their certainty is direct visual certainty.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r2.anchor: قدّم البصر هنا لأنهم كانوا يسمعون في الدنيا ويكذبون في الآخرة وأبصروا العذاب والحقيقة وقولهم يعني أنهم موقنون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p521/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p521/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p521/r4.claim: The Quran usually places hearing before sight because hearing is more central to instruction and communication, has shorter range, and develops before sight; a blind listener can still be taught, unlike a deaf person.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p521/r4.anchor: الأكثر في القرآن تقديم السمع على البصر لأن السمع أهم من البصر في التكليف والتبليغ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r1.claim: Though Quranic usage usually puts hearing first for its importance in instruction, shorter range, and earlier development, these passages put sight first for contextual reasons.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r1.anchor: الأكثر في القرآن تقديم السمع على البصر لأن السمع أهم من البصر في التكليف والتبليغ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r3.claim: The criminals heard reports of resurrection in life but doubted them; in the afterlife they see what they heard, gaining certainty through direct sight, so sight precedes hearing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p702/r3.anchor: الكلام عن المجرمين الذين كانوا في الدنيا يسمعون عن القيامة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r1.claim: If the address is to the Prophet, he would witness their helplessness at judgment in a degree beyond what he can imagine today.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r1.anchor: The implication is that the Prophet (sws) would have seen their helplessness at that time which he cannot even imagine today.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r2.claim: On the reading that the address is to the Prophet, the conditional sentence's suppressed result is eloquent: he would witness a helplessness beyond what he can imagine now.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r2.anchor: The answer to this conditional clause is suppressed and there is much eloquence in this suppression.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r3.claim: At judgment, the wrongdoers will admit that they now see and hear the truth, and ask to return for the chance to do good deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p143/r3.anchor: at that time everyone of these wrongdoers will confess that they fully see and accept and that they may be allowed to return

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r1.claim: المجرمون may mean the people who said أئذا ضللنا في الأرض, or the whole class of criminals to which they belong.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r1.anchor: وهم القائلون : ( أئذا ضللنا في الأرض ) أو جنس المجرمين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r2.claim: ناكسوا رؤوسهم means lowering their heads in shame and disgrace.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r2.anchor: ناكسوا رؤوسهم ( مطرقوها من الحياء والخزي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r3.claim: They are before their Lord at judgment, when the ugly deeds they committed in worldly life are exposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r3.anchor: عند ربهم ( حين حسابهم لما يظهر من قبائحهم التي أقترفوها في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r4.claim: The quoted plea is an utterance understood as a circumstantial clause governed by ناكسوا; this is better than supplying يستغيثون بقولهم.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r4.anchor: ومفعولا ربنا بتقدير القول الواقع حالا والعامل فيه ( ناكسوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r5.claim: They now perceive visible and audible signs and have the capacity to apprehend them, whereas before they were blind and deaf in the sense of failing to perceive anything.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r5.anchor: أي صرنا ممن يبصر ويسمع وحصل لنا الإستعداد لإدراك الآيات المبصرة والآيات المسموعة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r6.claim: They beg to be returned to worldly life so they can act righteously in light of the signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r6.anchor: وهذا على ما قيل إدعاء منهم لصحة مشعري البصر والسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r7.claim: One explanation is that the plea claims their faculties of sight and hearing are now sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r7.anchor: وهذا على ما قيل إدعاء منهم لصحة مشعري البصر والسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r8.claim: إنا موقنون may resume and explain the preceding plea, or stand as a resumption without intended causal force; either way it claims sound hearts and capacity to understand signs and act on them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r8.anchor: إنا موقنون 21 ( إستئناف لتعليل ما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r9.claim: Their declaration displays firmness in certainty and eagerness for it, which may explain why they do not add وأيقنا to أبصرنا وسمعنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r9.anchor: وفيه من إظهار الثبات على الإيقان وكمال رغبتهم فيه ما فيه وكأنه لذلك لم يقولوا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r10.claim: Sight precedes hearing because most promised righteous action follows hearing, so placing hearing last avoids interrupting that connection.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r10.anchor: ولعل تأخير السمع لأن أكثر العمل الصالح الموعود يترتب عليه دون البصر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r11.claim: One proposed sense is that they saw the resurrection they denied and its promised consequences, and heard the divine questioning of humans and jinn about messengers warning them of this day.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r11.anchor: بأن يقال : أبصرنا بالبعث الذي كنا ننكره وما وعدتنا به على إنكاره

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r12.claim: Another proposed sense is that they saw the resurrection and heard the messengers' words, now hearing them obediently and acknowledging them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r12.anchor: أو يقال أبصرنا البعث وسمعنا قول الرسل أي سمعناه سمع طاعة وإذعان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r13.claim: A further proposal is that they saw the ugliness of deeds they once considered good and heard angels tell them they would return to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r13.anchor: قبح أعمالنا التي كنا نراها في الدنيا حسنة وسمعنا قول الملائكة لنا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r14.claim: Another view says they saw God's messengers and heard their speech while still in worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا أبصرنا رسلك وسمعنا كلامهم حين كنا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r15.claim: A further view says they saw God's creative signs and heard revealed signs in worldly life, admitting that God had proof against them; the author calls this reading weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126#2/r15.anchor: أو أبصرنا آياتك التكوينية وسمعنا آياتك التنزيلية في الدنيا فلك الحجة علينا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r1.claim: The second-person address is phrased singularly but applies to every person capable of seeing.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r1.anchor: والخطاب في : ترى لكل واحد ممن يصح منه الرؤية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r2.claim: The horror would astonish any observer, even one used to extraordinary sights and calamities.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r2.anchor: إذ المراد بيان كمال سوء حالهم وبلوغها من الفظاعة إلى حيث لا يختص إستغرابها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r3.claim: Another explanation is that their state is so manifest that it cannot be hidden, so no particular observer is singled out.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r3.anchor: وقيل : لأن القصد إلى بيان أن حالهم قد بلغت من الظهور إلى حيث يمتنع خفاؤها البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r4.claim: The author says the estimated answer fits the first explanation about universal astonishment better; ترى is intransitive, with no expressed object.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r4.anchor: والجواب المقدر أوفق بما ذكر أولا والفعل منزل منزلة اللازم فلا يقدر له مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r5.claim: Another parse supplies an object from what follows: لو ترى المجرمين or their lowering of their heads.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يقدر لترى مفعول دل عليه ما بعد أي لو ترى المجرمين أو لو ترى نكسهم رؤسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r6.claim: A view addresses only the Prophet and reads لو as a wish that he could see the criminals, perhaps to rejoice at them; most grammarians say such a wish has no answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الخطاب خاصا بسيد المخاطبين صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r7.speaker: أبو حيان وابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan and Ibn Mālik insist that a wish expressed with لو requires an answer, citing al-Muhalhil's line about the buried Kulayb, where they construe لقر جوابا.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان وإبن مالك : لا بد لها من الجواب إستدلالا بقول مهلهل في حرب البسوس

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r8.claim: The author replies that al-Muhalhil's لو is conditional, not optative, and يخبر coordinates with an infinitive understood from نبش.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r8.anchor: ورد بأنها شرطية ويخبر عطف على مصدر متصيد من نبش

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r9.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r9.claim: Al-Khafājī offers a simpler account: when لو often carries a wish, it can take the wish construction's ruling, allowing omission of an unexpressed answer and an accusative answer.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r10.claim: The past forms in the counterfactual and إذ suit an event already realized in God's eternal knowledge, expressed as past by figurative usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r10.anchor: والمضي في لو الإمتناعية وإذ لأن أخباره تعالى عما تحقق في علمه الأزلي لتحققه بمنزلة الماضي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r11.speaker: أبو العباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r11.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās unusually reads the sentence as part of the command to say: Tell Muḥammad, if you could see the criminals; Abū Ḥayyān explains that he links it to يتوفاكم under the earlier قل.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p127/r11.anchor: ومن الغريب قول أبي العباس في الآية : المعنى قل يامحمد للمجرم ولو ترى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: An active participle for an action currently occurring or continuing functions like the present-tense verb in both meaning and government, taking its object in the accusative.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: فمعناه وعمله مثل هذا يضرب زيدا غدا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Poetic examples, including Zuhayr's تنوين on سابقا, show the active participle with tanwin in this ongoing-action use.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Dropping tanwin or the sound plural nun for ease does not change meaning or make the participle definite; its object then takes genitive as it is joined to the noun.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: فيحذفون التنوين والنون ولا يتغير من المعنى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Sībawayh cites ناكسو رؤوسهم as an active participle without its nun in annexation, with its object in the genitive.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: لو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءسهم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Qur'anic examples such as ذائقة الموت, مرسلوا الناقة, غير محلي الصيد, and آمين البيت الحرام illustrate the uninflected participle construction.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: هديا بالغ الكعبة and عارض ممطرنا show the participle remains indefinite without tanwin, since it can describe an indefinite noun.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: ويزيد هذا عندك بيانا قوله تعالى جده

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Al-Khalil gives هو كائن أخيك as a lightened form whose meaning is هو كائن أخاك.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: وقال الخليل هو كائن أخيك على الاستخفاف والمعنى هو كائن أخاك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Sībawayh cites non-tanwined participles in poetry by al-Farazdaq, al-Zibriqan, al-Sulayk, al-Nabigha, and al-Marrar as evidence for the construction.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: عيسى
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Isa reports that some reciters omit tanwin in Abu al-Aswad's verse to avoid two adjacent sukuns, not to make the participle genitive; Sībawayh calls this poetic necessity.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: When a participle and a second noun share its genitive complement, both may be genitive; accusative coordination is also possible by eliding an understood verb or participle.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: وتقول فى هذا باب هذا ضارب زيد

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Jarir and Ka'b ibn Juayl provide poetic examples of accusative coordination understood through an omitted verb or participle.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: If the action is completed rather than ongoing, the active participle has no tanwin and behaves like a noun, so a coordinated complement is genitive.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.anchor: أن الفعل قد وقع وانقطع فهو بغير تنوين ألبتة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: Accusative coordination becomes stronger after a long separation from the participle's complement; Sībawayh cites والشمس والقمر حسبانا as Qur'anic evidence.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوع.claim: With a participle governing two objects, tanwin allows either object order; without tanwin, the complement joined to the participle cannot be separated, as in مخلف وعده رسله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r10.claim: They bow their heads in shame and regret.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r10.anchor: {ناكسو رءوسهم} مطأطؤ رءوسهم، {عند ربهم} حياء وندما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r11.claim: One explanation has them admitting that they now see what they denied and hear the truth spoken by the messengers; another says they see their sins and hear what has been said about them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r11.anchor: {أبصرنا} ما كنا به مكذبين، {وسمعنا} منك تصديق ما أتتنا به رسلك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r12.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life so they can do righteous deeds, claiming certainty now.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r12.anchor: {فارجعنا} فأرددنا إلى الدنيا، {نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r13.claim: The answer to “if you saw” is suppressed, with the implied sense “you would see an astonishing sight.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r13.anchor: وجواب لو مضمر مجازه لرأيت العجب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r4.claim: The guilty lower their heads from shame and humiliation before their Lord.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r5.claim: They say they have seen what was promised and heard their Lord confirm His messengers; they ask to return to worldly life and act righteously because what they witnessed has removed doubt.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r5.anchor: إذ لم يبق لنا شك بما شاهدنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r6.claim: The answer to law is omitted, understood as “you would see something dreadful”; alternatively, law expresses a wish, with past tense in law and idh because what is certain in God's knowledge is like what has happened.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r6.anchor: وجواب { لو } محذوف تقديره لرأيت أمرا فظيعا

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r7.claim: Tarā needs no expressed object when it means seeing at that time; alternatively its object is supplied by what follows idh, and the address may be to the Prophet or anyone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r7.anchor: ولا يقدر ل { ترى } مفعول لأن المعنى لو يكون منك رؤية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r7.claim: The shift from addressing the criminals to addressing the Prophet consoles him and signals contempt for them; the address may also be to anyone capable of seeing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r7.anchor: عن خطابهم استهانة بهم وإيذانا بالغضب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r8.claim: The imperfect verb follows a particle normally associated with the past because the scene is certain, as though it already happened; this form lets listeners anticipate seeing the criminals' fate.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r8.anchor: لأنه لتحقق وقوعه كأن قد كان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r1.claim: “The criminals” are those who sever what God commanded to be joined.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r1.anchor: أي القاطعون لما أمر الله به أن يوصل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r2.claim: They bow their heads in shame, fear, humiliation, and abasement at the place of reckoning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r2.anchor: أي مطأطئوها خجلا وخوفا وخزيا وذلا في محل المناقشة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r3.claim: Their Lord is the benefactor who uniquely governs them.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r4.claim: They now see what they denied and hear God, the angels, and the fires, becoming certain of divine power and promises.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r4.anchor: ومن أصوات النيران وغير ذلك ما كنا نستبعده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r5.claim: They ask to be returned to the abode of earthly deeds so they can act righteously.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r6.claim: Their emphatic certainty answers their earlier doubt; witnessing the scene would reveal horror beyond description or human comprehension.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r6.anchor: مؤكدين لأن حالهم كان حال الشاك الذي يتوقف المخاطب في إيقانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r7.claim: They are not returned: divine beneficence had emboldened their disobedience, and valid faith must precede direct sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p55/r7.anchor: ولأن الإيمان لا يصح إلا بالغيب قبل العيان

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r3.claim: Qatada says the criminals see only when sight can no longer benefit them and hear only when hearing can no longer benefit them.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r5.claim: In a report about three divine explanations to Adam, God says that without His decree against lying, He would have shown mercy to Adam's descendants despite the severity prepared for them; the decree is to fill Hell with those who deny messengers and disobey, as 7:18 states.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله يعتذر إلى آدم يوم القيامة بثلاثة معاذير

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r6.claim: God says He will punish only descendants whom His prior knowledge showed would return to worse wrongdoing if sent back to worldly life, without repentance.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله يعتذر إلى آدم يوم القيامة بثلاثة معاذير

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r7.claim: God appoints Adam to judge at the scales: whoever's good outweighs evil by even an atom enters Paradise, demonstrating that only wrongdoers enter Hell.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله يعتذر إلى آدم يوم القيامة بثلاثة معاذير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.claim: “If you could see” expresses wonder at the unbelievers’ condition; the omitted consequence is more terrible because listeners fill it with their utmost imagining.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.claim: The criminals are unbelievers, as shown by the threat of Hell; their certainty now indicates they lacked it in worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.anchor: والمجرمون هم الكافرون بدليل التوعد بالنار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.claim: Their bowed heads express humiliation, despair, distress at punishment, and longing to return to earthly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.anchor: وتنكيس الرؤوس هو من الذل واليأس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.claim: The speech has an omitted introduction: they are saying, “Our Lord.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.anchor: وفي القول محذوف تقديره يقولون ربنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r5.claim: They now perceive what they were told in worldly life but denied; they seek return when it can no longer help.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360#2/r5.anchor: وقولهم أبصرنا وسمعنا أي ما كنا نخبر به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r1.claim: On Resurrection the polytheists stand humbled before God, heads bowed from shame; they say they now hear His words and obey His command, as in 19:38.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r1.anchor: حين عاينوا البعث، وقاموا بين يدي الله حقيرين ذليلين، ناكسي رؤوسهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r2.claim: They ask to return to worldly life to do good, now certain of God’s promise and meeting; if returned, they would again disbelieve and disobey, as 6:27–29 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r2.anchor: وقد علم الرب تعالى منهم أنه لو أعادهم إلى الدار الدنيا لكانوا كما كانوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r3.claim: Their later self-reproach says listening or reasoning would have kept them from the blazing Fire, as 67:10 states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p362/r3.anchor: لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير}

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r4.claim: Naks is turning something upside down; in illness it has ḍamma, while with kasra it denotes an arrow broken and reversed.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r4.anchor: النكس: قلب الشيء على رأسه، نكسه ينكسه، والنكس في المرض بضم النون، والنكس بكسر النون

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r7.claim: The apodosis of law is omitted; it may be supplied as “you would see a tremendous thing.”
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r7.anchor: جواب (لو) محذوف، تقديره: ولو ترى لرأيت أمرا عظيما

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r8.claim: Another proposed completion says the viewer would see something that prompts the utmost reflection.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r8.anchor: وقيل: لرأيت ما تعتبر به غاية الاعتبار

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r9.claim: Omitting the apodosis heightens the terror because the imagination can range over every possible consequence.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r9.anchor: وقيل: حذف جواب (لو)؛ لأنه أبلغ في التهويل؛ لأن القدر يذهب فيه كل مذهب

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r10.claim: A further analysis says the apodosis is implicit in the meaning of the surrounding words.

JISHUMI:v2p1086/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r1.claim: The verse shows that God judges His servants, disproving determinism: if all acts were created by God, judgment of people would be meaningless.
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r1.anchor: كانت مخلوقة لله تعالى لم يكن للحساب مع العباد معنى

JISHUMI:v2p1086/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r2.claim: Reward and punishment are deserved for acts of the heart as well as other acts.
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن الثواب والعقاب يستحق في أفعال القلوب.

JISHUMI:v2p1086/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r3.claim: God forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills; this passage does not specify who, a point clarified elsewhere.
JISHUMI:v2p1086/r3.anchor: وتدل على أنه يغفر لمن يشاء، ويعذب من يشاء،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r1.claim: Addressed to the Prophet, لو ترى expresses a wish that he see his enemies in their awful humiliation, as consolation for the harm they caused him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r1.anchor: أن يراد به التمني ، كأنه قال : وليتك ترى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r2.claim: Alternatively, لو is conditional and its apodosis is omitted: he would have seen a dreadful sight or the worst imaginable state.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r2.anchor: أن تكون لو الامتناعية قد حذف جوابها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r3.claim: The address may be generic, as in a saying about someone who repays kindness with harm, rather than directed to a particular listener.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r3.anchor: ويجوز : أن يخاطب به كل أحد ، كما تقول : فلان لئيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r4.claim: لو and إذ use past forms for a future scene because what God guarantees is certain; إذ is the time adverb for seeing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r4.anchor: ولو وإذ : كلاهما للمضي ، وإنما جاز ذلك ؛ لأن المترقب من الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r5.claim: Their plea receives no relief: they now see the truth of God's promise and threat and hear Him confirm His messengers; alternatively, they had been blind and deaf and now see and hear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r5.anchor: فلا يغاثون ، يعني : أبصرنا صدق وعدك ووعيدك وسمعنا منك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r6.claim: They ask to be sent back to worldly life.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r7.claim: A return would bring guidance by compulsion, but God made the matter one of choice; they chose blindness over guidance, so punishment fell on the blind rather than those who saw.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p517/r7.anchor: ولكننا بنينا الأمر على الاختيار دون الاضطرار

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r1.claim: They bow their heads while standing before their Lord at His reckoning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r2.claim: Ibn Isa says their heads are bowed from grief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r2.anchor: أحدها : من الغم ، قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara says their heads are bowed from humiliation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r3.anchor: الثاني : من الذل ، قاله ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r4.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash says their heads are bowed from shame.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r5.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says their heads are bowed from regret.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r5.anchor: الرابع : من الندم ، قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r6.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r6.claim: Ibn Isa says they saw the truth of God's warning and heard the messengers' confirmation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أبصرنا صدق وعيدك وسمعنا تصديق رسلك , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r7.claim: Qatada says they saw their sins and heard what was said about them, but only when sight and hearing could no longer benefit them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r7.anchor: الثاني : أبصرنا معاصينا وسمعنا ما قيل فينا , قال قتادة , أبصروا حين لم ينفعهم البصر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r8.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life to do righteous deeds there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r8.anchor: أي ارجعنا إلى الدنيا نعمل فيها صالحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r9.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r9.claim: Al-Naqqash says they now affirm the Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says they now affirm that what Muhammad brought is true.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r10.anchor: الثاني : مصدقون بالذي أتي به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه حق , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r11.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r11.claim: Sufyan says God refutes their request by saying that if they were returned, they would revert to what they had been forbidden; he cites 6:28.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p358/r11.anchor: قال سفيان : فأكذبهم الله فقال : ^ { ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه }

MUQATIL:32:12-14/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:12-14/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:12-14/r1.claim: The criminals are Meccan unbelievers, who bow before God and plead to return to worldly life to do good because they are certain of resurrection.
MUQATIL:32:12-14/r1.anchor: { ولو ترى } يا محمد { إذ المجرمون } يعني عز وجل كفار مكة { ناكسوا رءوسهم عند ربهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r1.claim: The address may be to the Messenger or anyone; لو is counterfactual, with an omitted answer meaning one would see a tremendous scene.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r1.anchor: الخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو لكل أحد ولو امتناعيه والجواب محذوف أى لرايت أمرا عظيما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r2.claim: The criminals are those who asked whether they would really be recreated after being lost in the earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r2.anchor: هم الذين قالوا أئذا ضللنا فى الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r3.claim: إذ refers to the future because what God promises is treated as already present; it is adverbial to ترى.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r3.anchor: ولو واذ للمضى وانما جاز ذلك لأن المترقب من الله بمنزله الموجود

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r4.claim: They bow their heads from humiliation, shame, and regret.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r5.claim: At their Lord means at His reckoning; pause here because an omitted phrase is understood: they say the following words.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r5.anchor: عند حساب ربهم ويوقف عليه لحق الحذف اذ التقدير يقولون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r6.claim: They either see the truth of God's promise and threat and hear His confirmation of messengers, or say they were blind and deaf and now see and hear.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r6.anchor: صدق وعدك ووعيدك وسمعنا منك تصديق رسلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r7.claim: They ask to return to worldly life and do good, meaning faith and obedience.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p291/r8.claim: They now claim certainty about resurrection and reckoning.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r1.claim: The clause beginning “if you saw” is a subject with its predicate supplied by the following construction, according to Qurtubi.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسوا رءوسهم عند ربهم } ابتداء وخبر

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the address to the Prophet is also an address to his community: Muhammad would see the deniers of resurrection on Judgment Day and witness an astonishing scene.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: والمخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مخاطبة لأمته. والمعنى: ولو ترى يا محمد منكري البعث

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r3.speaker: أبو العباس
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r3.claim: Abu al-Abbas proposes that Muhammad is told to say to a criminal that, if he saw the criminals bowing their heads before their Lord, he would regret his past conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r3.anchor: ومذهب أبي العباس غير هذا، وأن يكون المعنى: يا محمد، قل للمجرم ولو ترى إذ المجرمون

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r4.claim: Their bowed heads express regret, disgrace, grief, humiliation, and anguish.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r4.anchor: «ناكسو رءوسهم» أي من الندم والخزي والحزن والذل والغم

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r5.claim: They are before their Lord at the reckoning and recompense for their deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r5.anchor: «عند ربهم» أي عند محاسبة ربهم وجزاء أعمالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r6.claim: “Our Lord” introduces what the criminals are saying.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r6.anchor: «ربنا» أي يقولون ربنا. «أبصرنا» أي أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r7.claim: They now see what they used to deny and hear what they used to reject.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r7.anchor: «أبصرنا» أي أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب. «وسمعنا» ما كنا ننكر

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r8.claim: An alternative gloss says they saw the truth of God's threat and heard confirmation of His messengers.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r9.claim: They see and hear when those faculties can no longer benefit them; in worldly life they perceived but failed to reflect, as though blind and deaf, then awakened in the hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r9.anchor: أبصروا حين لا ينفعهم البصر، وسمعوا حين لا ينفعهم السمع. «فارجعنا» أي إلى الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r10.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r10.anchor: «فارجعنا» أي إلى الدنيا. { نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون }

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r11.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r11.claim: Al-Naqqash says they now affirm belief in the resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r11.anchor: أي مصدقون بالبعث قاله النقاش. وقيل: مصدقون بالذي جاء به محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r12.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r12.claim: Yahya ibn Salam says they now believe that Muhammad brought the truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r12.anchor: مصدقون بالذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه حق قاله يحيى بن سلام

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r13.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r13.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says God refutes their request with the statement that, if returned, they would relapse into what they were forbidden to do and would be lying.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r13.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري: فأكذبهم الله تعالى فقال: ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r14.claim: Another explanation makes their certainty the removal of doubts: they had seen and heard in life but did not reflect, and only now became alert.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r14.anchor: وقيل: معنى «إنا موقنون» أي قد زالت عنا الشكوك الآن وكانوا يسمعون ويبصرون في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r15.claim: A further reading takes their words as admitting that they saw God's messengers and marvels of creation and heard the messengers, leaving them without an excuse before they request return.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:12/r15.anchor: وقيل: أي ربنا لك الحجة، فقد أبصرنا رسلك وعجائب خلقك في الدنيا، وسمعنا كلامهم
